text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Syrian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hafez al-Assad sends two letters to Sultan Qaboos (of Oman) and the emir of Bahrain regarding the Arab position and developments of the Middle East peace process. Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam says: "We are not besieged with a sole option to surrender to Israel...and our Arab brothers support us."
- U.S. President Bill Clinton says there is no peace without a settlement on the Syrian-Israeli track and Washington's efforts will focus on resumption of the peace talks.
- Political and media circles say Israel is feeding violence and tension in the region and is working to impose surrender on Arabs.

- Assad discussed with European Middle East envoy Miguel Angel Morations the European role to revive the peace process and said Syria is committed to the basis of the process and the resulted agreements. Assad says: "We welcome the European commitment to play a positive and effective role to achieve just and comprehensive peace."
- Syrian Ambassador to Washington Walid al-Mua'lem says talks should resume from the point at which they stopped and there are no secret contacts or exchange of letters between Syria and Israel.
